sources.citation: Dürr, Michael. 1987. A Preliminary Reconstruction of the Proto-Mixtec Tonal System. Indiana 11: 19-61. Berlin: Ibero-Amerikanisches Institut. doi:10.18441/ind.v11i0.19-61
sources.note: Comparative reconstruction of Proto-Mixtec tone (two registers *high/*low in four tonemic couplets plus final glottal stop and a 'tone modification' sandhi feature) over 17 dialects, one of which is Chayuco ('Jamiltepec (pueblo Chayuco)', Pensinger 1974). Chart 3 (pp. 23-24) gives the Chayuco reflexes of the basic couplets in a three-level high/mid/low notation: *high-high(') > mid-mid, *high-low > mid-low, *low-high > low-mid; p. 27 places Chayuco in 'dialect area A' (San Miguel, Atatlahuca, Ocotepec, Molinos, Cacaloztepec, Xayacatlán, Chayuco, Silacayoapan, Mixtepec, Alacatlazala, Cahuatach…

tone.quote: 17) Jamiltepec (pueblo Chayuco) (Jam): Pensinger (1974) [p. 36] ... There is a high degree of correspondence between the reflexes in the dialects San Miguel, Atatlahuca, Ocotepec, Molinos, Cacaloztepec, Xayacatlán, Chayuco, Silacayoapan, Mixtepec, Alacatlazala, Cahuatache and Metlatonoc. These dialects form dialect area A. The dialects Peñoles, Jicaltepec, Diuxi and Coatzospan show a clearly distinct system. The reflex of *low-low is at a higher level in the register than that of *high-high. The couplets changed places. These dialects will be called area B. [p. 27]
tone.locator: p. 36 (dialect list, item 17) and p. 27 (sec. 1.1, dialect areas); Chart 3 on pp. 23-24

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra. 2024. Rates of change and phylogenetic signal in Mixtec tone. Language Dynamics and Change 14(1): 1-41. doi:10.1163/22105832-bja10031
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with restricted access (login, paywall or limited view)
sources.note: 'I created a database of tonal and segmental sound changes across a sample of 42 Mixtec languages. I calculated phylogenetic signal with the metric D and estimated rates of change.. The results show that the majority of tone changes show phylogenetic signal and that they generally do not change at a faster rate than segments.' Likely includes the Chayuco tone-change codings (reflexes of Proto-Mixtec *H/*L) but gives no dedicated description of the Chayuco system.
